Characters in Romeo and Juliet.The Nurse: Juliet's talkative caretaker, who raised her, carries messages between the lovers and is one of the play's comic voices.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Lord Capulet: Juliet's father threatens to disown her if she refuses to marry Paris.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Lady Montague: Romeo's mother dies of grief after her son is exiled, a death reported late in the play.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Prince Escalus: The ruler of Verona, whose name echoes the real Della Scala family, threatens death to anyone who breaks the peace again.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Ophelia: Hamlet's doomed love interest comes from a different tragedy, set in Denmark rather than Verona.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Desdemona: Othello's wife, who dies over a lost handkerchief, belongs to a different tragedy.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Viola: The shipwrecked heroine of Twelfth Night, who disguises herself as a man, is not in this play.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Orsino: The lovesick duke of Illyria in Twelfth Night opens his play with 'If music be the food of love'.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Malvolio: The pompous steward of Twelfth Night is tricked into yellow stockings by a forged love letter.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Rosalind: The heroine of As You Like It disguises herself as a boy in the Forest of Arden.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Orlando: The wrestler-lover of As You Like It carves love poems on trees, so he is from a comedy, not Verona.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Puck: A mischievous fairy from A Midsummer Night's Dream, so from a different play entirely.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Lysander: A young lover in A Midsummer Night's Dream who is bewitched by a love potion, not in Verona.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Hermia: Hermia of A Midsummer Night's Dream defies her father to love Lysander, so not Verona.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Cressida: Cressida belongs to Troilus and Cressida, a play about the Trojan War.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Portia: The wise heroine of The Merchant of Venice, who rescues Antonio with legal cleverness.
Characters in Romeo and Juliet.Bassanio: Portia's suitor in The Merchant of Venice borrows money to woo her.

Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Tweedledum: The rhyme's duo, drawn by Tenniel, agree to fight over a spoiled rattle until a monstrous crow scares them off.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Tweedledee: Alice meets the identical twins in the woods, where they recite the long poem The Walrus and the Carpenter.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Humpty Dumpty: He insists words mean whatever he chooses; the nursery rhyme never says he is an egg, but Alice notes how much he looks like one.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Red Queen: She tells Alice that you must run as fast as you can just to stay in place, a line that inspired the 'Red Queen' idea in biology.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.White Queen: She lives backward, feels pain before pricking her finger, and says she has believed six impossible things before breakfast.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.White Knight: This gentle, bumbling inventor with odd gadgets is often read as a self-portrait of Carroll.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Jabberwock: Carroll's nonsense poem about slaying this beast gave English words like 'chortle' and 'galumphing'.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Red King: He sleeps through the book; Tweedledee tells Alice she is just a thing in his dream, and would vanish if he woke.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.The Walrus: In the poem, he weeps sympathetically for the oysters while eating as many as he can, a masterclass in crocodile tears.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.The Carpenter: Walrus's partner in the poem: they lure young oysters on a beach stroll and then eat nearly all of them.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.The Lion: He fights the Unicorn for the crown, as in the old nursery rhyme, and says plum cake must be shared before it's cut.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.The Unicorn: Another old rhyme figure who fights the Lion, and who thinks Alice must be a monster, just as she thinks him one.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Cheshire Cat: That grin that remains after the cat fades belongs to the first book, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, not the mirror sequel.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.White Rabbit: Wonderland begins with this watch-checking rabbit, but the sequel starts with kittens and a chess game.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Queen of Hearts: The tyrant of the first book's card-themed court; the sequel's queens are chess pieces instead.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Caterpillar: The hookah-smoking creature asks Alice 'Who are you?' in Wonderland; the looking-glass world gives her a gnat instead.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Dodo: Carroll based the Dodo on himself; he stammered his surname Dodgson as 'Do-Do-Dodgson'. It's in the first book only.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Mock Turtle: Mock turtle soup was a real Victorian imitation of turtle soup, made from calf's head; this sad creature is in Wonderland.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Gryphon: The Gryphon, part eagle and part lion, escorts Alice to the Mock Turtle, but only in the first book, Wonderland.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Duchess: Tenniel's grotesque duchess, with her pepper-filled kitchen and baby that turns into a pig, belongs to Wonderland.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Dormouse: He falls asleep at the Mad Hatter's tea party and gets stuffed into the teapot, in the first book.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Tinker Bell: Barrie's fairy speaks only in a tinkling bell sound; she belongs to Neverland, not either Alice story.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Peter Pan: Barrie gave the rights to this boy who wouldn't grow up to Great Ormond Street Hospital; he never visits Alice.
Characters in Through the Looking-Glass.Dorothy: Dorothy is L. Frank Baum's Kansas girl in Oz; in the book her magic shoes are silver, only the film made them ruby.

Artists who died before 1700.Leonardo da Vinci: Leonardo died in France in 1519, and fewer than 20 paintings are securely attributed to him.
Artists who died before 1700.Michelangelo: Michelangelo always insisted he was a sculptor first, yet he painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling in about four years.
Artists who died before 1700.Raphael: Raphael died at just 37 in 1520, but left behind The School of Athens and a huge workshop.
Artists who died before 1700.Rembrandt: He died in 1669, after going bankrupt in 1656 and selling off his huge art collection.
Artists who died before 1700.Vermeer: Only around 35 paintings are firmly attributed to him, and he died in 1675 leaving his family in debt.
Artists who died before 1700.Caravaggio: He fled Rome after killing a man in a brawl in 1606 and died in 1610 on his way back.
Artists who died before 1700.Rubens: Besides painting, Rubens was a diplomat, and was knighted by both Spain and England; he died in 1640.
Artists who died before 1700.Titian: The Venetian master died in 1576, probably of plague, in his late eighties or older.
Artists who died before 1700.Botticelli: His Birth of Venus fell out of fashion after his death in 1510, and was rediscovered in the 19th century.
Artists who died before 1700.Hieronymus Bosch: He died in 1516, and fewer than 30 paintings survive of his strange visions, including The Garden of Earthly Delights.
Artists who died before 1700.Albrecht Dürer: He drew a famous 1515 rhinoceros woodcut without ever seeing the animal; he died in 1528.
Artists who died before 1700.Velázquez: Velázquez's Las Meninas, painted for Philip IV of Spain, puzzles viewers about who is looking at whom; he died in 1660.
Artists who died before 1700.El Greco: Born in Crete, Domenikos Theotokopoulos was nicknamed 'The Greek', settled in Toledo and died in 1614.
Artists who died before 1700.Hans Holbein: The German portraitist of Henry VIII died in London in 1543, probably of plague.
Artists who died before 1700.Claude Monet: Claude Monet, whose Impression, Sunrise gave Impressionism its name, died in 1926, long after 1700.
Artists who died before 1700.Van Gogh: Van Gogh painted nearly all his famous work in his last decade, sold few works in his lifetime, and died in 1890.
Artists who died before 1700.Pablo Picasso: Picasso lived until 1973 and produced an enormous number of works, so he's far too late for this list.
Artists who died before 1700.Francisco Goya: Goya died in France in 1828, well over a century after the cutoff, so he doesn't belong on this list.
Artists who died before 1700.J. M. W. Turner: Turner, the master of light and storms, died in 1851, a century and a half too late for this list.
Artists who died before 1700.John Constable: John Constable painted the English countryside, as in The Hay Wain, and died in 1837, far after 1700.
Artists who died before 1700.Fragonard: Fragonard, the rococo painter of The Swing, died in 1806, long after 1700.
Artists who died before 1700.Delacroix: Delacroix painted Liberty Leading the People in 1830 and died in 1863, so he's far too late.
Artists who died before 1700.Gustav Klimt: Klimt, of The Kiss and its gold leaf, died in 1918, many generations after 1700.
Artists who died before 1700.Salvador Dalí: Dalí, the melting-clocks surrealist, died in 1989, so he's as modern as it gets for this list.

Car brands named after a person.Ford: Henry Ford's moving assembly line, introduced in 1913, cut the Model T's build time from over twelve hours to about ninety minutes.
Car brands named after a person.Ferrari: Enzo Ferrari began as a racing driver and ran Alfa Romeo's race team before putting his own name on a car in 1947.
Car brands named after a person.Porsche: Ferdinand Porsche designed the original Volkswagen Beetle; his son Ferry built the first car to carry the Porsche name in 1948.
Car brands named after a person.Lamborghini: Ferruccio Lamborghini made tractors first. Legend says he began building sports cars after Enzo Ferrari brushed off his complaints about a clutch.
Car brands named after a person.Chevrolet: Louis Chevrolet was a Swiss-born racing driver who co-founded the company in 1911, then left it within a few years.
Car brands named after a person.Dodge: Brothers John and Horace Dodge first supplied parts to Ford, and held Ford shares, before launching their own cars in 1914.
Car brands named after a person.Honda: Soichiro Honda's company started with motorcycles in 1948, and he began his career by making piston rings.
Car brands named after a person.Citroën: André Citroën's double-chevron logo mirrors the V-shaped teeth of the herringbone gears his first company made.
Car brands named after a person.Peugeot: The Peugeot family business dates to the early 1800s, and it still makes pepper mills and coffee grinders as well as cars.
Car brands named after a person.Renault: Brothers Louis, Marcel and Fernand founded the company in 1899. Louis had built his first car at age 21 in a garden shed.
Car brands named after a person.Maserati: The trident logo comes from the Neptune statue in Bologna's Piazza Maggiore, home of the Maserati brothers' first workshop.
Car brands named after a person.Bentley: Founder W.O. Bentley built aircraft engines in World War I, and his cars won Le Mans five times in the 1920s and early 1930s.
Car brands named after a person.McLaren: Bruce McLaren, a New Zealander, founded the racing team in 1963 and died testing a car in 1970 at just 32.
Car brands named after a person.Tesla: Named after inventor Nikola Tesla, not its famous boss: Elon Musk joined in 2004 as an investor, after others had founded it.
Car brands named after a person.Jaguar: Jaguar is the big cat, not a founder. The company began in 1922 as the Swallow Sidecar Company before adopting the name.
Car brands named after a person.Volkswagen: The name is German for 'people's car', from 1930s Germany, so no founder's surname is hidden in it.
Car brands named after a person.Subaru: Subaru is Japanese for the Pleiades star cluster, and the six stars in its logo represent the merged companies behind the brand.
Car brands named after a person.Volvo: Volvo is Latin for 'I roll', first chosen for a ball-bearing brand, so there is no Mr. Volvo.
Car brands named after a person.Lexus: Lexus is an invented word. Toyota launched the luxury brand in 1989, and it honors nobody.
Car brands named after a person.Fiat: Fiat stands for Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino, and it is also Latin for 'let it be done'. No founder's name appears.
Car brands named after a person.Saab: Saab is an acronym for Svenska Aeroplan Aktiebolaget, since the company began as a Swedish aircraft maker.
Car brands named after a person.Kia: Kia is usually explained as meaning 'rising from Asia', so it names an ambition, not a person.
Car brands named after a person.Nissan: Nissan is short for 'Nippon Sangyo', meaning Japan Industries, so it is a corporate name, not a surname.
Car brands named after a person.Hyundai: Hyundai is the Korean word for 'modern', so it is a statement of intent, not a founder's name.

Add 'air' in front to make a word.Port: Airport traffic is huge: Atlanta's airport has long been the busiest in the world, handling over 90 million passengers a year.
Add 'air' in front to make a word.Plane: Americans say airplane, while British English keeps aeroplane; the Wright brothers called their craft a flying machine.
Add 'air' in front to make a word.Ship: Airship was the name for dirigibles, and the Hindenburg disaster of 1937 effectively ended the era of passenger airships.
Add 'air' in front to make a word.Craft: Aircraft covers everything from balloons to jets, and it counts as both singular and plural.

Words that go before 'station'.Train: The first railway stations appeared in the 1830s; Liverpool Road in Manchester, opened 1830, is the oldest surviving passenger one.
Words that go before 'station'.Bus: Big coach stations are often multi-level hubs; London's Victoria Coach Station has handled national routes since 1932.
Words that go before 'station'.Police: In many countries the local police station doubles as the place where you report a lost passport or wallet.
Words that go before 'station'.Fire: Early fire stations kept horses harnessed and ready; the first 'fire pole' was installed in a Chicago station around 1878.
Words that go before 'station'.Gas: In the US it's a gas station, but in the UK the same place is a petrol station, a classic word difference.
Words that go before 'station'.Space: The International Space Station circles Earth about every 90 minutes, so its crew sees around 16 sunrises a day.
Words that go before 'station'.Radio: Radio stations get call letters: in the US, those east of the Mississippi usually start with W and those west with K.
Words that go before 'station'.Power: A big power station's cooling towers release steam, not smoke, which is why they look like they're billowing clouds.
Words that go before 'station'.Weather: Weather stations record temperature, pressure, wind and rain, and some have kept unbroken records for over 150 years.
Words that go before 'station'.Polling: Polling stations are often schools and community halls, which is why voting day can close a school for the day.
Words that go before 'station'.Petrol: The word petrol dates to the late 19th century, and in the US the same fuel is simply gasoline.
Words that go before 'station'.Lifeboat: In the UK, lifeboat stations are run by a charity, the RNLI, which is funded by donations and crewed largely by volunteers.
Words that go before 'station'.Charging: Electric-vehicle charging stations come in speeds; the fastest can add hundreds of kilometers of range in about 20 minutes.
Words that go before 'station'.School: A school station isn't a thing: 'station' needs a function like boarding or broadcasting, which schools don't fit.
Words that go before 'station'.Hospital: Hospitals have 'nurses' stations' inside them, but 'hospital station' on its own isn't a normal phrase.
Words that go before 'station'.Bank: You can find a bank branch on the street, but not a 'bank station'; the word 'bank' pairs with 'holiday' or 'account'.
Words that go before 'station'.Church: Churches have 'stations of the cross', but a church station is not the usual phrase.
Words that go before 'station'.Farm: Farm station sounds right to Australians: a 'station' there is a huge sheep or cattle farm, though it doesn't pair here.
Words that go before 'station'.Hotel: Hotel is a place to stay, not a 'station'; the closest common phrase is 'train station hotel'.
Words that go before 'station'.Library: Libraries do have a 'librarian's station', but 'library station' isn't a phrase.
Words that go before 'station'.Zoo: Zoos don't have a 'station' in everyday speech, even though they do have feeding times.
Words that go before 'station'.Museum: A museum can have an 'interactive station', but 'museum station' mostly appears as a subway stop name.
Words that go before 'station'.Prison: Prison, like jail, can't take 'station': you go to a police station and then to prison.
Words that go before 'station'.Castle: Castle station sounds plausible but isn't a common phrase, though many castles do sit near a train stop.

Easter traditions and treats.Egg hunt: Hiding eggs goes back to German customs of the 1500s. The White House has hosted an annual egg roll on its lawn since 1878.
Easter traditions and treats.Easter bunny: The bunny arrived in America with German immigrants in the 1700s, who told children an egg-laying hare called Osterhase would leave eggs in nests.
Easter traditions and treats.Hot cross bun: The cross on top is said to mark Good Friday. An old English rhyme and tradition claims buns baked that day never go moldy.
Easter traditions and treats.Chocolate egg: The first hollow chocolate eggs appeared in Europe in the early 1800s. Cadbury made its first ones in 1875.
Easter traditions and treats.Egg rolling: Rolling eggs down a hill is said to echo the stone rolling from Christ's tomb. Races are held in Britain, Germany and at the White House.
Easter traditions and treats.Simnel cake: This British fruitcake is topped with eleven marzipan balls, standing for the apostles minus Judas. It dates back to medieval times.
Easter traditions and treats.Easter bonnet: New hats for Easter were once seen as good luck. New York's Fifth Avenue Easter Parade made fancy bonnets famous in the 1800s.
Easter traditions and treats.Palm Sunday: The Sunday before Easter recalls Jesus entering Jerusalem as crowds waved palm branches. Churches often hand out palm fronds.
Easter traditions and treats.Good Friday: Despite its mournful meaning, it's called 'Good' in English, possibly from an older sense of 'holy'. It marks the crucifixion.
Easter traditions and treats.Easter lily: This white trumpet-shaped flower symbolizes purity and resurrection. Growers time it to bloom for Easter, and it is toxic to cats.
Easter traditions and treats.Peeps: These marshmallow chicks, first made by hand in 1953, took 27 hours each. Machines now make one in about six minutes.
Easter traditions and treats.Egg dyeing: Dyeing eggs is an ancient spring custom. Ukrainian pysanky use wax-resist, much like batik, to create intricate patterns.
Easter traditions and treats.Candy cane: The striped hook is a Christmas sweet, said to be shaped like a shepherd's crook. Easter's sweets are eggs, bunnies and marshmallow chicks.
Easter traditions and treats.Pumpkin pie: Pumpkin pie belongs to American Thanksgiving. Traditional recipes spice the filling with cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg.
Easter traditions and treats.Yule log: The Yule log, a log burned or a chocolate roll cake, is a midwinter and Christmas tradition.
Easter traditions and treats.Dreidel: Spun during Hanukkah, the dreidel is a game of chance. Players win or lose tokens depending on which letter lands face up.
Easter traditions and treats.Latke: Potato pancakes fried in oil are a Hanukkah food. The oil recalls the miracle of the temple lamp.
Easter traditions and treats.Mince pie: A British Christmas treat. Old versions held minced meat as well as fruit, and the name stuck even though modern ones are sweet and meatless.
Easter traditions and treats.Valentine: A card or sweetheart for February 14, not Easter. The holiday honors one or more early Christian martyrs named Valentine.
Easter traditions and treats.Shamrock: A shamrock is Irish and tied to St. Patrick's Day on March 17. Easter sometimes lands close by, but the clover has no part in it.
Easter traditions and treats.Fruitcake: Dense and loaded with soaked fruit, a well-made fruitcake can keep for months or years. It is a Christmas cake, not an Easter treat.
Easter traditions and treats.Gingerbread man: A Christmas biscuit. Gingerbread people are often credited to Queen Elizabeth I, who had them made as likenesses of guests.
Easter traditions and treats.Advent wreath: This wreath has four candles lit week by week before Christmas, so it counts down to December 25, not toward Easter.
Easter traditions and treats.Candy apple: Candy apples are an autumn fair and Halloween treat. They were reportedly invented in 1908 by a New Jersey candymaker.

Day of the Dead traditions.Marigold: Marigolds, called cempasúchil, are believed to guide spirits home with their vivid color and strong scent. Petal paths lead from streets to altars.
Day of the Dead traditions.Ofrenda: An ofrenda is a home altar laden with photos, food, candles and the favorite things of the dead, built to welcome their spirits each autumn.
Day of the Dead traditions.Pan de muerto: This sweet bread is decorated with crossed bone-shaped strips and often scented with orange blossom or anise. It is baked for the holiday.
Day of the Dead traditions.Papel picado: Papel picado is tissue paper cut into lacy patterns and strung overhead. The fluttering paper stands for the wind and the fragility of life.
Day of the Dead traditions.Calavera: Calavera means 'skull', and also names short satirical verses mocking the living as if already dead. Printmaker José Guadalupe Posada made them famous.
Day of the Dead traditions.La Catrina: La Catrina is an elegant skeleton in a fancy hat, created by Posada around 1910 to mock Mexicans who aped European high society.
Day of the Dead traditions.Copal: Copal is a tree resin burned as incense since Aztec and Maya times. Its smoke is believed to carry prayers and guide souls.
Day of the Dead traditions.Skeleton: Skeletons here are festive, not scary. Dressed up, dancing and playing guitars, they show that death is a natural part of life.
Day of the Dead traditions.Jack-o'-lantern: Carved pumpkin lanterns are a Halloween tradition from Ireland, while the Mexican celebration has marigolds and altars.
Day of the Dead traditions.Piñata: Piñatas are smashed at Mexican parties and Christmas posadas. It's Mexican, but belongs to celebrations other than the Day of the Dead.
Day of the Dead traditions.Mistletoe: Mistletoe is hung at Christmas for kisses. It is a December custom from northern Europe, nothing like Mexico's autumn remembrance.
Day of the Dead traditions.Egg hunt: Egg hunts are an Easter tradition in spring, with children collecting hidden eggs, and have no link to the autumn Day of the Dead.
Day of the Dead traditions.Dreidel: A dreidel is a spinning top played at Hanukkah in December with coins or chocolate, and it has no part in the Day of the Dead.
Day of the Dead traditions.Shamrock: The shamrock is a St. Patrick's Day emblem for Ireland in March, not a Mexican autumn symbol.
Day of the Dead traditions.Cupid: Cupid is a Valentine's Day figure who fires arrows of love in February, which has nothing to do with this remembrance of the dead.
Day of the Dead traditions.Red envelope: Red envelopes of money are a Chinese New Year gift for good luck, not a Day of the Dead custom.
Day of the Dead traditions.Rangoli: Rangoli are colored floor designs made for Diwali in India. They resemble Day of the Dead flower carpets, but they are Indian.
Day of the Dead traditions.Cornucopia: The cornucopia is a Thanksgiving harvest symbol, a horn overflowing with food, not a Day of the Dead one.
Day of the Dead traditions.Maypole: The maypole is danced around on May Day in spring, as a European festival of growth, not death.
Day of the Dead traditions.Tinsel: Tinsel is a shiny Christmas tree decoration. Day of the Dead altars use marigolds and papel picado instead.
Day of the Dead traditions.Lederhosen: Lederhosen are Bavarian leather shorts worn at Oktoberfest, so they are tied to Germany, not Mexico.
Day of the Dead traditions.Witch hat: The witch's pointed hat is a Halloween costume piece, a different holiday from the Day of the Dead, though they share a date.
Day of the Dead traditions.Candy cane: Candy canes are a Christmas treat, hung on trees in December, while Day of the Dead tables hold sugar skulls and pan de muerto.

College football bowl games.Alamo Bowl: San Antonio's bowl, started in 1993 and named for the famous mission where the 1836 battle occurred.
College football bowl games.Gator Bowl: Jacksonville's bowl since 1946, infamous for the 1978 game when coach Woody Hayes punched an opposing player.
College football bowl games.Liberty Bowl: Memphis has hosted it since 1965; it began in Philadelphia in 1959 and has a patriotic name.
College football bowl games.Holiday Bowl: San Diego's bowl, founded in 1978 and known for high-scoring games in the Southern California sun.
College football bowl games.Sun Bowl: El Paso's bowl dates back to 1935, which makes it one of the oldest bowl games in the country.
College football bowl games.Super Bowl: The NFL's championship is a pro game, not a college bowl; its name was reportedly inspired by a toy 'Super Ball'.
College football bowl games.Pro Bowl: The NFL's all-star game is a pro contest, held in Hawaii for decades, not a college bowl.
College football bowl games.Dust Bowl: The 1930s drought and dust-storm region of the Great Plains, no football game, though its name fits the pattern.
College football bowl games.Punch Bowl: A party container for drinks, nothing to do with football beyond sharing a word.
College football bowl games.Fishbowl: Goldfish memory is better than the myth of three seconds, but a fishbowl is certainly no football game.
College football bowl games.Salad Bowl: Salinas Valley in California is nicknamed the 'Salad Bowl of the World' for its lettuce, not a football game.
College football bowl games.Mixing Bowl: Just a kitchen tool; the name 'bowl game' comes from the shape of the Rose Bowl stadium, not from kitchens.
College football bowl games.Soup Bowl: People have shaped bowls from clay for many thousands of years, but this one is not a football game.
College football bowl games.Hollywood Bowl: An outdoor amphitheater in Los Angeles famous for its shell stage; despite the 'bowl' it is a concert venue.
College football bowl games.Cereal bowl: Corn flakes began in the 1890s as a health food at a Michigan sanitarium, but this bowl is no football game.
College football bowl games.Dog bowl: Animal Planet's annual Puppy Bowl parody has run since 2005, but it is no real bowl game.
College football bowl games.Toilet bowl: Fans nickname a clash of two bad teams a 'toilet bowl', but it is no official bowl.
